# GitHub Copilot instructions for sensor-ingestion

This is a **CamelBee-generated Apache Camel microservice** (QUARKUS, Java 21). Generated by the [CamelBee MCP Server](https://www.camelbee.io/mcp) — treat existing code as the source of truth, all tests pass out of the box.

## Primary guidance

**Read `AGENTS.md` in the repo root first.** It contains the full architecture, testing requirements, and critical rules. This file is a short pointer so Copilot users get the essentials without Copilot having to follow cross-file references.

## Architecture (3-layer)

- **Consumer** (`src/main/java/.../routes/consumer/{technology}/`) — entry points; unmarshal + validate + map API → Domain
- **Central** (`routes/central/`) — orchestration; fan-out to backends
- **Producer** (`routes/producer/{technology}/`) — map Domain → Infra + call backend

Models flow: `model/api/` → `model/domain/` → `model/infra/`. Mappers are MapStruct.

## Non-negotiable rules

- First line of every route's `configure()`: `camelBeeRouteConfigurer.configureRoute(this)`
- Consumer routes use `errorHandler(genericExceptionHandler.appErrorHandler())`
- Central / producer routes use `errorHandler(noErrorHandler())`
- Every route has `.routeId()`; every backend endpoint in central routes has `.id()`
- Never call a backend from a consumer — always go through the central route
- REST is contract-first: keep the `rest().openApi().specification("openapi/<your-api>.yaml").missingOperation("ignore")` binding in the REST consumer. Change the API by editing the OpenAPI spec (renaming the spec file is fine — update the path in this binding and in pom.xml `<inputSpec>`) — never hand-define endpoints with `rest().get(...)` / `rest().post(...)`
- Transform, don't reinvent: when replacing the domain, every file keeps its existing mechanism and structure (spec bindings, MapStruct mappers, choice routes) — rename domain nouns and edit specs; a transformed file should diff as a rename, not a rewrite
- Before ANY domain transformation, read the full checklist at `.claude/skills/cb-replace-domain/SKILL.md` — it enumerates all ~40 touchpoints (specs, mappers, routes, all three test levels, fixtures, compose env vars). Do not attempt a transformation from the prompt alone
- Hand-written model classes set as exchange body MUST have a meaningful `toString()` (Lombok `@ToString` is fine); the CamelBee tracer and debugger UI depend on it
- Integration and black-box tests start ALL backends via the single compose-based `DockerComposeContainer ENV` in `TestContainerConfiguration` (`compose-backends.yml` / `compose-blackbox.yml`, `--compatibility`). Never add backend-specific TestContainers classes (`PostgreSQLContainer`, `KafkaContainer`, `GenericContainer`, `@ServiceConnection`, ...). The generated tests already passed with this setup — if a test fails, debug your change, not the container infrastructure
- Before deleting or rewriting ANY generated file (especially during a domain transformation): baseline the pristine scaffold first — `git init && git add -A && git commit -m "chore: initial camelbee scaffold" && git tag camelbee-baseline`, or a plain folder copy if git is unavailable
- This project ships ALL three test levels out of the box: `src/test`, `src/integration-test`, `src/black-box-test`. Never conclude a test level "does not exist" — if a folder is missing or empty, it was deleted; restore it from `camelbee-baseline` and transform it with the main code
- Quarkus: `.marshal(jacksonDataFormat)` not `.marshal().json()`; `componentModel = "cdi"` in MapStruct; `method(this, "x")` over lambdas in `.split()`; register new model classes in `config/ReflectionConfig.java` for native builds

## Testing — all three levels, both success and error

Every new operation or backend change requires:
- Unit tests (`src/test/`) — AdviceWith mocks
- Integration tests (`src/integration-test/`) — TestContainers with real backends
- Black-box tests (`src/black-box-test/`) — Docker Compose end-to-end

Skipping success scenarios is not acceptable. Run in order: `./mvnw test` → `./mvnw jacoco:prepare-agent failsafe:integration-test failsafe:verify` → `./mvnw verify -Pblack-box-test`.

## Backend credential alignment

Every backend's credentials are repeated in **four** places and must agree:
1. `src/integration-test/resources/compose-backends.yml` (what the backend container accepts)
2. `src/main/resources/application.yml` (app reads these on host)
3. `src/black-box-test/resources/compose-blackbox.yml` (overrides when app runs in Docker — uses internal Docker service name + internal port)
4. `src/black-box-test/java/utils/DataVerifier.java` / `DataSeeder.java` / `MessageVerifier.java` (test JVM on host — uses `localhost` + published port)

Rule: files 2 and 3 use Docker service names; file 4 uses `localhost:<published-port>`. All four must share the same credentials.

## Generated code — do not edit

Models under `model/api/json/`, `model/api/xml/`, `model/api/proto/`, `model/api/avro/`, `model/infra/*`, SOAP/gRPC stubs: all generated at build time from specs in `src/main/resources/`. Edit the spec, run `./mvnw generate-sources`.
